name: Start-Simple Complexity Gate — Decision Table
purpose: Recommend, for an incoming task, whether direct execution or some level of orchestration is the proportionate starting point. The table is a design artifact for proposal D4 in docs/orchestrator-improvements-plan.md; it is not loaded by any runtime code.

recommendationBoundary.produces: A recommendation only: direct-execution-candidate, orchestrate-candidate, orchestrate-serialized, orchestrate-with-review, or collect-facts.
neverProduces: Runtime enforcement or hard blocking of any command or delegation
A decision the user cannot override
recommendationBoundary.override: Every recommendation can be overridden by an explicit user decision; the gate never silently changes how a task is executed.
recommendationBoundary.evidence: Recommendations are advisory guidance produced from task facts; they carry no verification power until the evaluation protocol in d4-evaluation-template.json is run and results are collected.

dimensions.label: Independent subtasks
dimensions.question: How many child tasks could run with disjoint read/write scopes and no dependency on one another?
dimensions.sourceReference: docs/orchestrator-improvements-plan.md D4 (independent subtasks); src/core/policy.ts DELEGATION_RULES parallelSafe

dimensions.label: Dependent stages
dimensions.question: How many sequential steps must complete in order (e.g., schema change before prompt wiring before tests)?
dimensions.sourceReference: docs/orchestrator-improvements-plan.md D4 (dependent stages); D1 proposal (dependency IDs, topological execution)

dimensions.label: Files/modules touched
dimensions.question: How many files or modules are expected to change, and do any writers overlap?
dimensions.sourceReference: src/core/policy.ts orchestrationRules (disjoint write scope, serialize overlapping implementation)

dimensions.label: Independent review needed
dimensions.question: Should a separate reviewer audit the change before it is reported complete (default require_review=true already demands this for orchestrated runs)?

dimensions.label: External side effects
dimensions.question: Does the task reach outside the working tree — network, remote repositories, GitHub, worktrees, services, or the published package?
dimensions.sourceReference: src/opencode-v2/github tools, src/opencode-v2/worktree; docs/orchestrator-improvements-plan.md D4 (external side effects)

dimensions.label: Shared mutable state
dimensions.question: Would parallel writers contend for the same file, module, generated artifact, or storage key?
dimensions.sourceReference: src/core/policy.ts orchestrationRules (no two children claim the same file or area); WORKTREE_BOUNDARY_GUIDANCE (prompt-level rules do not enforce isolation)

dimensions.label: Security/compliance risk
dimensions.question: Does the change touch credentials, redaction, secrets handling, permission semantics, worktree roots, or remotely mutating tools?
dimensions.sourceReference: src/core/policy.ts SECRET_HANDLING_GUIDANCE; src/opencode-v2/process/redact.ts; docs/orchestrator-improvements-plan.md D4 (security/compliance risk)

dimensions.label: Expected value of parallelism
dimensions.question: Would running children concurrently save meaningful wall-clock time versus the added model cost, coordination, and failure surface?
dimensions.sourceReference: docs/orchestrator-improvements-plan.md D4 (expected parallelism value); D1 scaling heuristics (breadth-first tasks justify more workers only when expected value justifies cost)

unknownHandling.policy: If any dimension is unknown at admission time, the gate must not guess: it recommends collect-facts (read-only exploration or a direct user question) before classification.
unknownHandling.appliesTo: every dimension; an unknown high-risk or shared-state dimension must not be treated as 'no'.

high-risk.definition: Security/compliance risk or external side effects with material blast radius are present.
high-risk.note: Highest precedence: any high-risk signal wins over shared-state, multi-step, or trivial signals.

shared-state.definition: Parallel writers would contend for the same mutable files, modules, generated artifacts, or storage keys.
shared-state.note: Serialized orchestration keeps disjoint write scopes enforced per stage; parallelizing overlapping writers is not recommended.

multi-step.definition: Multiple dependent stages or several mostly-independent subtasks across more than a couple of files, with no high-risk or shared-state signal.
multi-step.note: Orchestration is a candidate because coordination buys decomposition and a maker-checker review; parallelism only when expected_parallelism_value is medium or high.

trivial.definition: One file, one or two local edits, no review obligation, no external side effects, no shared or security concerns.
trivial.note: Matches README.md:30 — skip the orchestrator for single-file trivial edits.

incomplete-facts.definition: One or more dimensions cannot be assessed from the request.
incomplete-facts.note: Precondition for classification: when facts are incomplete the gate emits collect-facts before applying any other precedence rule, and reclassifies only when the missing facts are known.

precedenceRules.rationale: Guessing can under-delegate hidden complexity or over-delegate trivial work; exploration is cheaper than either error.

precedenceRules.condition: security_compliance_risk = true OR (external_side_effects = true AND blast radius is material)
precedenceRules.rationale: High-risk changes must be planned and independently reviewed before completion.
Overlapping writers must be serialized or isolated; prompt-level rules do not enforce filesystem isolation.
Coordination adds value when work decomposes or stages depend on each other.

precedenceRules.condition: single file, no side effects, no shared state, no security concern, no review obligation
precedenceRules.rationale: README.md:30 already advises prompting the model directly for such edits.
Ambiguity between labels resolves conservatively toward gathering facts, not toward a guessed label.

decisionOutcomes.meaning: Read-only exploration (planning/research roles) or a direct user question before recommending an execution path.
Prompt the model directly, no delegation; the README default for trivial single-file edits.
Orchestration is appropriate; parallelize only when expected_parallelism_value is medium/high and write scopes are disjoint.
Orchestrate with implementation serialized across overlapping writable scopes.
Orchestrate and require an independent reviewer pass before reporting completion (require_review=true default).

sourceReferences.note: Advises skipping the orchestrator for single-file trivial edits — the direct-execution candidate rule.
Defines the eight dimensions and the recommendation semantics this table formalizes.
max_parallel integer 1..8 default 4 — the ceiling context for parallelism-value reasoning.
orchestrationRules(): prompt-guidance-only constraints (disjoint write scopes, serialize overlapping implementation, review before completion). This table inherits the same advisory boundary.
WORKTREE_BOUNDARY_GUIDANCE / MANAGED_WORKTREE_GUIDANCE: prompt rules and managed worktrees do not provide atomic child isolation — shared-state serialization is required, not assumed.
Directional evidence on multi-agent cost and the value of decomposition; cited by the parent plan, not a validation of this table.
Directional evidence on orchestration patterns; the secondary '64% single-agent sufficiency' claim must be validated independently before use.

designOnlyStatement: This artifact is design-only: it makes no runtime changes, is not referenced by plugin code, enforces nothing, and contains no measured results or telemetry.
